PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 01/25/30 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening shortness of breath and persistent cough with increased sputum production.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up after two days of continued outpatient management. He reports a significant decline in his respiratory status since his last visit, with a notable increase in the frequency and volume of his productive cough, which now yields copious amounts of yellowish-green sputum. He describes his dyspnea as worsening, particularly during minimal exertion, and he experiences increased fatigue, which he attributes to both his respiratory condition and the ongoing corticosteroid therapy.
The patient expresses concern regarding the mild epigastric discomfort, which has persisted despite the initiation of Omeprazole. He denies any episodes of hematemesis or melena but admits to occasional heartburn. Mr. Fairfax also reports that he has been experiencing intermittent fevers, with temperatures reaching 100.5F, and he continues to have night sweats.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, + intermittent fevers, + night sweats, - weight loss. Pulmonary - + worsening productive cough with increased yellowish-green sputum, + significant dyspnea, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - + persistent mild epigastric discomfort, + heartburn, - nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 125/80 mmHg - Heart Rate: 88 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 28 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 85% on supplemental oxygen (6 L via nasal cannula).
General: The patient appears fatigued and is in moderate respiratory distress, utilizing accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Marked wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with rhonchi; crackles audible throughout lung fields, more pronounced in the lower lobes.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender; mild epigastric discomfort noted; no hepatosplenomegaly.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with worsening bacterial pneumonia, evidenced by increased respiratory symptoms and insufficient improvement since last assessment. 2. Persistent hypoxemia requiring close monitoring of oxygen therapy; slight deterioration in oxygen saturation noted. 3. Fatigue likely exacerbated by systemic steroid therapy and unresolved respiratory pathology, with persistent mild gastrointestinal discomfort possibly related to Prednisone and heartburn.
PLAN
1. Change antibiotic therapy to oral Levofloxacin 750 mg once daily for 7 days to target potential resistant organisms; monitor for clinical response in 48 hours. 2. Continue oral Prednisone at 60 mg daily, with plans to taper further as tolerated; continue Omeprazole 20 mg daily to manage gastric irritation. 3. Maintain supplemental oxygen at 6 L via nasal cannula; consider increasing to 8 L if oxygen saturation does not improve; evaluate the need for BiPAP if respiratory distress escalates. 4. Schedule a repeat chest X-ray today to assess for progression or resolution of pneumonia; obtain a sputum culture to guide further antibiotic therapy if necessary. 5. Continue nebulized bronchodilator therapy (Albuterol) every four hours as needed; increase frequency if wheezing persists; consider adding Ipratropium bromide to enhance bronchodilation. 6. Schedule a follow-up visit within 48 hours to reassess respiratory status, medication efficacy, and gastrointestinal symptoms; discuss the potential for pulmonary rehabilitation once stabilized.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax remains under close observation in the internal medicine unit. The treatment team will continue to modify the management plan based on his clinical progress, particularly focusing on his respiratory function and gastrointestinal symptoms. Patient education regarding the importance of adherence to the new antibiotic regimen and the need to report any new or worsening symptoms will be emphasized during this visit.
